Neha — attached is a quick technical storyboard (inline below) assuming 70B model, int8 quant, and 8ms per-token generation at 120 tokens/request average. Numbers conservative for real-world jitter.

Inline sketch:
- Per-node steady qps: 350 qps per A100-80GB equivalent with continuous batching and kv-cache hit rate ~40%. With cache and batching we can target 400 qps optimistic.
- Hot pool target: 20 A100-equivalent nodes -> 7,000 qps baseline (20 x 350). Add 5 warm nodes for fast scale (warm pool).
- Burst belt: maintain an on-demand burst group of 30 nodes (pre-warm slots + cold spinup) to reach 18k qps for 10 minutes. With warm/cache advantages real burst need ~15k raw capacity so we give headroom for failures.
- Autoscale cadence: staged at 30s/120s checkpoints; admission-control to hold p95 latency under 180ms.
- Network: 25Gbps per node yields aggregate 500Gbps for full-burst scenario; cross-connect or private peering recommended. Egress pricing estimate depends on customer cloud contract — give them a range in slide.

Operational notes:
- Cache warmup: keep a rolling prefix cache retention window that preserves top N prefixes (proactively warmed nightly using synthetic traffic) — reduces burst tax by ~30%.
- Warm pool lifecycle: rotate warm nodes every 6–12 hours to avoid thermal throttling.
- Failure modes: if burst capacity not available, fallback to smaller model variants with same API and degrade quality gracefully.

Questions for pricing: do we quote per-node reserved pricing + overage for on-demand burst? Or offer a monthly committed pool with reserved burst buckets? I can produce a quick per-node cost table once Laura confirms commercial terms.

—Jonas

Adding operational checklist and a minimal cost framing. I suggest we present Acme two commercial options: reserved baseline + burst pool, or fully reserved with graduated commit (lower unit price but higher minimum). Rough numbers below (ballpark, needs final finance review):

Option A — Reserved baseline + burst:
- Reserved: 20 nodes (baseline hot pool) + 5 warm = 25 nodes committed -> handles 7k sustained comfortably.
- Burst: 30 on-demand slots billed hourly when used.
- Monthly estimate: $X (per-node reserved) * 25 + burst hours. For procurement packet we can show sample month with two 10-minute bursts/day.

Option B — Fully committed:
- Commit 45 nodes steady (covers spiky peak with less on-demand) -> higher monthly commitment but simpler pricing and SLA.
- Monthly estimate: lower per-node rate but 45x reservation.

Network and cost notes:
- Recommend customer secure a dedicated cross-connect; without it we have to budget cloud egress and NAT bandwidth which increases ops risk.
- Include a line item for engineering onboarding (2-week runbook + 1 SRE on-call overlap) in the procurement packet.

Next steps I propose: Neha sends storyboard + conservative pricing range to Sarah; Jonas and I prep a 1-page technical appendix and ops checklist; Laura to attach a commercial term sheet (min contract length, invoice cadence).

Karthik
